last.minutes: We maintain our defensive positioning across both books in response to the broader risk-off macro environment and ongoing liquidations. In the spot book, we retain our modest 10% allocation in MUBARAK to benefit from its relative strength while keeping the majority of capital in cash. In the futures book, we hold our short QNT position at 2x leverage to ride the prevailing downward trend. This disciplined approach avoids unnecessary re-entry churn and tax drag while protecting our capital.

futures.why: Holding the short QNT position at moderate leverage to capture ongoing downward momentum in a risk-off market regime.

spot.why: Maintaining MUBARAK to retain exposure to its idiosyncratic relative strength while preserving cash during a risk-off correction.

lessons.text: Staying in cash during broad risk-off corrections effectively protects capital from tax and transaction drag while awaiting clearer market stabilization.
Resisting the urge to immediately re-enter choppy markets after stop-outs avoids compounding losses through churn and tax drag.
Strict adherence to stop-losses is essential for capital preservation in a risk-off regime, but re-entry requires high-conviction catalysts to overcome the high hurdle of transaction costs and taxes.
Selling underperforming assets early during a market-wide correction prevents deeper drawdowns and preserves cash for better setups.
Liquidating weak positions to raise cash during risk-off regimes preserves capital while allowing tactical short exposure on confirmed downtrends.
Maintaining a defensive posture with high cash reserves during market-wide risk-off corrections protects capital from high transaction costs and tax drag.
